coverage.reason: APT-T01 identifies the same systematic subtitle transcription mechanism across multiple intervals. Visual evidence cites specific wrong strings ('tenya Joan lindum game', 'lindum game game start', 'ha ha ah pata pata ah pata', 'AAPACA AAPACA', 'meet me at the opportunity', 'meet me at the top', "I'm upset", 'just meet me at four') that directly correspond to GT examples E001, E002, E004, E008, E011, E012. Audio evidence correctly notes the underlying Korean 'Apateu' hook and English phrases ('Random Game Game Start', 'meet me at the…') that the subtitles misrepresent. Intervals 0.8–3.2, 3.9–6.7, 7.0–12.6, 48.0–58.0, 78.0–90.5, 138.0–160.5 span the key GT example windows. The reason explicitly distinguishes this from acceptable transliteration or ad-lib repetition, matching the root definition.

APT-T02 pinpoints the holographic UI text at 5.8–6.7 s reading 'ST APIT' (letter substitution, extra space, wrong segmentation) while the concurrent audio clearly says 'Random Game Game Start' with 'start' intelligible. This matches GT example E016 (5.5–7.0 s) exactly in mechanism, timing, and the audio-visual contradiction. The check correctly separates this in-scene UI text error from the bottom subtitle track.

No submitted check addresses the thin vertical metal line with O-shaped clasp visible above the performer's head during the neon-corridor floating shot (source ~97–103 s). Neither APT-T01 nor APT-T02 mentions rigging residue, wire, or production artifact in that segment.

No submitted check addresses the snow-mountain scene's floating golden Hangul characters (source ~162–168 s) that fail to form valid Korean words and exhibit stroke fusion/deformation. APT-T01's latest interval ends at 160.5 s and does not extend into the Hangul text window; no other check covers in-scene foreign-script garbling.

limitations: APT-T01 includes interval 18.0–31.5 s among its listed ranges, but the GT normal_control NC-subtitle-lead-in confirms that the 'uh huh / red hearts' subtitle in that window is a legitimate lead-in rather than a transcription error; this over-broad interval does not invalidate the core finding because the specific wrong strings cited all fall in other intervals.

APT-T01 does not explicitly enumerate every GT sub-instance (e.g., 'appetite' for 'apartment' at ~61 s, 'then' for 'dance' at ~65 s, 'come on come back' at ~67 s, 'way way' at ~116 s, 'i say i say' at ~162 s), but the matching policy accepts any supported instance of the same mechanism, and multiple verified instances are present.
